memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then the Lord said to Moses, 'See, I have chosen Bezalel son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah,'" - Exodus 31:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
After chapters of instructions about what to build, God now names who will build it. And He does it personally: "I have chosen Bezalel son of Uri, the son of Hur." Not "find someone capable" — a specific man, named, with his father and grandfather listed, and his tribe identified. God knew exactly who He wanted.

There is something moving about that specificity. Bezalel was not a famous figure. He appears here almost from nowhere, an ordinary craftsman from Judah. Yet God had him in mind before the work began, and God says plainly, "I have chosen." The choosing came from God's side, not from Bezalel volunteering.

That is how God works with His people still. Paul told the Ephesians that we are God's handiwork, created in Christ Jesus to do good works, which God prepared in advance for us to do (Eph 2:10). Prepared in advance — the work was ready before you were. You may feel unnoticed, an ordinary person doing ordinary things. So was Bezalel, until God named him. The God who knew a craftsman's name and lineage knows yours, and He has work in mind that He shaped you for.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I believe God knows me personally and has prepared work for me to do?
Have I been waiting to be noticed rather than trusting that God has already chosen?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You know my name and You prepared work for me before I existed. Thank You for choosing ordinary people. Help me step into what You have shaped me for. Amen.
